title: Renting in Tamil Nadu: Your Rights and the Rent Authority
summary: How Tamil Nadu's rent law protects tenants and landlords, and how to register a rent agreement.
keyPoints: Always keep a signed copy of the agreement and receipts for rent and deposit.
Pay rent by bank transfer, so there is a record.
The deposit is a security, not extra rent, and must be returned after lawful deductions.
A landlord cannot lock you out or cut water or electricity to force you to leave.
For a dispute, approach the Rent Authority or the civil court, not self-help.
sectionRefs: Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017

body.text: If you rent a house or a shop in Tamil Nadu, both you and the owner have clear rights. A written, registered agreement keeps most problems away.
📘 Which law applies in Tamil Nadu

items: Tamil Nadu has its own law: the Tamil Nadu Regulation of Rights and Responsibilities of Landlords and Tenants Act, 2017. It provides for a Rent Authority to register tenancy agreements and to decide rent disputes.
The Model Tenancy Act, 2021 is a central model law. States adopt it in their own way, so the exact rules depend on the State law in force.
Very old tenancies may still be governed by the older Rent Control law. Check which law applies to your agreement.

body.text: State rent rules and their notification can change. Before you rely on any rule, check the current position on the Tamil Nadu government website or with a lawyer.
🔑 What the rent agreement should say

items: Rent, the due date and how it is paid (bank transfer is best, so there is a record).
The security deposit amount and when it will be returned.
The notice period for leaving, or for asking a tenant to leave.
Who pays maintenance, electricity, water and property tax.
Who does small repairs, and who does structural repairs.
The deposit is a security, not extra rent. It should be returned after lawful deductions when you vacate.
Under the Model Tenancy Act, the deposit is capped at 2 months' rent for residential premises and 6 months for commercial premises.
Any deduction must be explained, with bills or receipts.
Rent can be increased only as the agreement or the law allows, usually with proper notice.
A tenant must give written notice before leaving, as agreed.
A landlord must give written notice before asking a tenant to leave, and must have a valid ground such as non-payment of rent or genuine need.
Eviction must follow the legal process. A landlord cannot lock a tenant out or cut water or electricity to force an exit.

body.text: 📌 Where to go if there is a dispute

items: Approach the Rent Authority set up under the State rent law, or the civil court, whichever applies.
Keep the signed agreement, rent receipts and deposit proof ready.
For free legal help, contact your District Legal Services Authority (helpline 15100).

body.text: Always keep a signed copy of the agreement and receipts for rent and deposit. Papers settle most rent disputes.

practicalSteps: Put the rent, deposit, notice period and repair duties in a written, signed agreement.
Pay rent by bank transfer and keep the receipts.
Register the agreement with the Rent Authority if the law requires it.
For a dispute, approach the Rent Authority or the civil court, not self-help.
exceptions: Different rules can apply to commercial premises, to agricultural land and to very old tenancies.
The exact State position and its notification should be checked before you rely on it.

faqs.q: Can the landlord keep my deposit for normal wear and tear?
faqs.a: No. A deposit can be adjusted only for unpaid dues or actual damage beyond normal use, as set out in the agreement.

faqs.q: Do I need to register the rent agreement?
faqs.a: Under the State law a tenancy agreement may need to be registered with the Rent Authority. Ask the Rent Authority or a lawyer about your case.

misconceptions.myth: A landlord can throw a tenant out at any time.
misconceptions.fact: No. Eviction must follow the agreement and the law, with written notice and a valid ground.
